I love that he said this. If it was from any other dev, I might question it but I've followed the development of Ark for quite some time now. A significant number of user suggestions were implemented in to the game over the course of the last year. There was a point when you couldn't go more than a day or two without seeing big feature-laden updates to the client and the server, and this continued for many months.

Ark isn't perfect, but the community involvement definitely shows in the game. It's an example of early access done right. It can not only be beneficial to the customers, but it can also pay off big for the developers. If you like open world survival, Ark is definitely one of the games that is best in class.

I think that's an excellent perspective. I haven't played it yet, but following the early access news is like I'm getting a peek into the active development of a game as it matures. If I want to wait for the stable release, I'm free to do that. Too often nowadays, I'll buy a game that is already a "stable" release and feel like I'm still witnessing the middle of its development cycle, which isn't what I want. I've got to appreciate the way the Ark devs are managing their early access development.
It's actually very stable right now, but I couldn't blame anyone for being cautious. In an early access release, stable today might be broken tomorrow.

That's encouraging to hear nonetheless :) I'm just waiting for stable because I've got a low bandwidth cap and can't afford to play a game until the frequent updates start to slow down. That's what bugs me most about buying a game and having it continue development post-launch. Halo: Master Chief Collection needed a 15GB day one update, and Payday 2: Crimewave Edition had multiple 9GB updates shortly after it released. I don't mind optional DLC that I can decline to download if I'm close to my cap, but it sounds like Studio Wildcard is doing a good job of working on core development and gathering player feedback prior to stable release, which is exactly how early access should be.
